observations: PRED-1601.H3 ('a fourth stanza about idleness that has no Greek counterpart') contradicts the earlier states of the otium chain (PRED-1049.H1, PRED-1051.H1). It sits in an anticipatory-erratum 'First Edition, Reconstructed from Its Corrections' (#1601), whose apparatus note 6 says the line 'has now been pushed past its evidence and withdrawn twice (#1598, #1600)'; the contradiction may be deliberate structure. It is placed last in the states set by registration date; a later pass may judge whether the text's own claim to be a first edition puts it first.

PRED-1598.E1 (TP35.2, 'The interpretation advanced in the forthcoming work has been withdrawn') belongs with PRED-1601.H3 (TP35.1): both are in the Sappho Wrote the Dinosaurs anticipatory-erratum line, and 1598.E1 is already related to PRED-1624.E1.

PRED-1483.H4 (set with PRED-283.H7 as Catullus-is-κῆνος) also carries the otium chain's invertibility claim ('invertible for exactly that reason, as lossy compression is not'), which belongs with PRED-1049.H1.
PRED-1486.H3 ('Catullus occupies the reader-seat (line 1)') restates the Catullus-is-κῆνος claim (PRED-283.H7, PRED-1483.H4) inside a distinct two-seat claim about Catullus and Philo; left unset.

PRED-1411.H2 summarizes the otium chain (#1048, #1049, #1051, #1052, #1053) as Catullus being the 'transmission instrument' by which 'the fifth stanza's opening survives in Greek'; left out of the states set as a later summary, not a state.
